subject.title: fix(acp): close shared state database on gateway shutdown (#100637)

question: Should this focused ACP shutdown PR be repaired as the canonical fix for the SQLite handle leak, or should maintainers prefer a broader shared SQLite cache lifecycle fix such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100827?
rationale: The code defect is clear, but the permanent lifecycle owner is a maintainer boundary choice because sibling PRs split between ACP shutdown wiring, event-ledger close contracts, and cache-owner exit hooks.

options.title: Repair this focused ACP PR
options.body: Fix the post-timeout write-after-close gap, add real ACP shutdown or hot-reload proof, then re-review this branch as the candidate canonical fix.

options.title: Prefer the broader cache-owner PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100827 after its blocker is fixed if maintainers want SQLite cache owners rather than ACP server shutdown to own end-of-life cleanup.

options.title: Pause until one canonical path wins
options.body: Hold this PR and sibling contributor PRs until maintainers pick the lifecycle boundary, then close or supersede the non-canonical candidates with links.

recommendation.title: Repair this focused ACP PR
recommendation.body: Fix the post-timeout write-after-close gap, add real ACP shutdown or hot-reload proof, then re-review this branch as the candidate canonical fix.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ACP SQLite metadata and shared-state history makes this the strongest routing candidate for the lifecycle-boundary decision.
